//: TwoPointFive config. JSON has no comments, so every option is documented by the
//_: "//name" line directly above it (those keys are ignored by the loader). Delete a
//__: line entirely to fall back to its default. Values below are this machine's settings.
//resolution: 540p | 600p | 720p | 900p | 1080p | 1440p | native  —  fullscreen CPU render-target size, letterboxed to the screen; the biggest perf lever (default 720p; ignored in windowed mode)
//renderScale: 0.25 .. 2.0  —  multiplies the render size on both axes (0.5 = quarter the pixels; >1 supersamples). Applies fullscreen and windowed (default 1.0)
//windowed: true | false  —  decorated resizable window instead of borderless fullscreen (default false)
//windowWidth: integer > 0  —  window size AND render size in windowed mode; ignored fullscreen (default 1280)
//fovDegrees: 70 .. 130  —  horizontal field of view at the 16:10 reference aspect; wider displays get more side view, not squash (default 100)
//hudScale: 0.25 .. 2.0  —  sizes the status bar + debug text (1.0 = original 320x200 proportions filling screen height). Weapon has its own knob (default 1.0)
//weaponScale: 0.25 .. 2.0  —  sizes the first-person weapon viewmodel, independent of hudScale (default 1.0)
//vsync: true | false  —  true = tear-free FIFO present; false = mailbox (uncapped, low-latency) when the driver offers it (default true)
//maxFPS: integer >= 0  —  frame-rate cap (a sleep at end of frame) used only when vsync is off; 0 = uncapped (default 0)
//renderer: software | hardware  —  software = the CPU rasterizer (lightingMode below picks vanilla vs enhanced); hardware = GPU-geometry path: the level is built into GPU geometry and the GPU does texturing, depth, the sector fade, per-surface dynamic point lights (torches/muzzle flash/rockets/plasma), HDR + bloom, and 3D voxel models. Needs a working Vulkan driver; auto-falls back to software (with a loud log line) if it can't start. Default software.
//lightingMode: enhanced | vanilla  —  enhanced = CPU emits a G-buffer + Vulkan does deferred lighting/HDR/bloom; vanilla = CPU shades every wall/flat, GPU only blits. Auto-falls back to vanilla if the GPU path won't start (default enhanced)
//lightScale: 0.1 .. 2.0  —  multiplies every sector's authored light before shading; lower = darker (default 0.75)
//exposure: 0.1 .. 4.0  —  final multiply on the enhanced pipeline's HDR colour before the tonemap; ignored by vanilla mode (default 1.0)
//shadows: true | false  —  enhanced pipeline's screen-space shadows for the nearest dynamic lights; no effect in vanilla mode (default true)
//groundShadows: true | false  —  cheap contact-shadow blob on the floor under every thing and the player, both pipelines (default false)
//fogColor: hex "RRGGBB" (leading # ok)  —  distance-fog colour. Empty (default) disables fog. Works in all three render paths (software vanilla/enhanced, hardware)
//fogDensity: 0 .. 0.02  —  exponential distance-fog strength: fogFactor = 1 - exp(-density * distance) in map units. 0 (default) = off. ~0.0006 a light haze, ~0.003 a heavy murk. Fog is only applied when fogColor is also set
//textureQuality: nearest | bilinear | trilinear | aniso2x | aniso4x | aniso8x | aniso16x  —  one global texture filter for walls, flats, sprites and voxels. nearest = classic hard pixels (fastest). The filtered modes are CPU-heavy: ~5x the frame cost at trilinear, ~8x at aniso8x/16x (1080p). Unknown -> nearest (default nearest)
//voxels: true | false  —  replace map-object sprites with voxel models from assets/voxel/Doom{1,2}_Voxel.pk3 where a model exists; harmless if the pack is absent (default true)
//flashlight: true | false  —  enables the F-key head-mounted flashlight (a forward beam in enhanced/hardware, a flat brightness bump in vanilla) (default true)
//voxelScale: 0.25 .. 4.0  —  map units per voxel; Cheello's Voxel Doom is authored at 1.0 (default 1.0)
//quake1Textures: true | false  —  layer a Quake 1 texture pack (assets/textures/quake1/, built by `go run ./tools/importquake` from assets/import/Quake1_Textures.pk3) over the hi-res set: a Quake texture wins for every Doom name the curated table covers, all others fall through to assets/textures/walls|flats then the WAD. Leaves the existing hi-res PNGs untouched (default false)
//switchWeaponOnPickup: true | false  —  true = auto-switch to a newly picked-up weapon (id's behaviour); false = keep the current one up (default true)
//skill: 1 .. 5  —  which map THINGS spawn (1 = ITYTD, 3 = HMP, 5 = Nightmare). Only spawn counts differ; no ITYTD half-damage / Nightmare fast+respawn (default 3)
//damageScale: 1 .. 100000  —  percent of vanilla damage the PLAYER takes (100 = normal, 50 = half, 1 = near-invincible). Crushers ignore it (default 100)
//music: true | false  —  load and play each level's background track (default true)
//weaponVolume: 0.0 .. 2.0  —  loudness of weapon sounds relative to the rest of the SFX. A literal 0 means "unset" -> 1.0, so use e.g. 0.02 for near-silent (default 1.0)
//worldVolume: 0.0 .. 2.0  —  loudness of level machinery (doors, lifts, floors, crushers, switches). Same 0 caveat as weaponVolume (default 0.5)
//showDebugInfo: true | false  —  top-left FPS / XYZ / angle text overlay (default true)
//showStatusBar: DEPRECATED — superseded by hudStyle. Kept only so an old config with showStatusBar:false (and no hudStyle) still hides the HUD
//hudStyle: doom | quake2 | none  —  doom = the full bottom status bar; quake2 = minimal corner HUD (big health bottom-left, ammo bottom-right, armour above health, keys top-right); none = no HUD. F1 cycles them in-game (default doom)
//crosshair: off | dot | cross  —  centre-screen aiming marker; scales with resolution, hidden while dead (default dot)
//crosshairSize: tiny | small | medium | large  —  scales the crosshair; medium is renderHeight/240 (default medium)
//iwad: path string  —  explicit base IWAD, only consulted when the WAD you pick is a PWAD. Empty = auto-find next to the PWAD / up its parents (default "")
//map: "E1M5" | "MAP07" | ...  —  map marker to start on, case-insensitive. Empty = ask when the WAD has >1 map, else the conventional first level (default "")
//invertMouseY: true | false  —  true = push the mouse forward to look down (flight-stick convention) (default false)
//mouseSensitivity: 0.0002 .. 0.02  —  radians of view rotation per pixel of raw mouse motion, both axes (default 0.0022)
//turnSpeed: 0.5 .. 10.0  —  keyboard turn rate (Left/Right arrows) in radians per second (default 2.5)
//alwaysRun: true | false  —  true = move at run speed by default, hold Shift to walk (default false)
